solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brazilian ready to follow team of stars

parts.note: the real is Brazil's currency, and ready (money) is cash

explanation.surface: A Brazilian footballer is poised to join an all-star team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazilian' looks like a player, but with 'ready' it means Brazilian cash: 'ready' is slang for money, and Brazil's unit is the real.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal is the astronomers' adjective for things relating to the stars, as in sidereal time.

clue.text: Severely affected hand nurse holds

indicators.note: what holds something has it inside

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A nurse holds a hand that has been badly hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN, a State Enrolled Nurse, is an old British nursing grade and a crossword stock nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To be smitten is to be struck hard, by illness or by love.

clue.text: Remixed vocal edit for Life of Riley

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a recording, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sound engineer remixes a vocal track for a song called Life of Riley.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-studio words are all mechanism; the answer is the Italian 'sweet life'.
explanation.definitionFit: La dolce vita, the sweet life, is a life of carefree ease, which is what living the life of Riley means.

clue.text: Uneasy setter's supporting others

indicators.note: in a down clue the support sits underneath

parts.note: the setter says I'VE for 'the setter has'

explanation.surface: A nervous setter props up everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is 'I', so 'setter's' is I'VE, with the apostrophe standing for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive means restless and fidgety, uneasy under restraint.

clue.text: Foolish time to start to climb up tree

parts.note: April 1st, April Fools' Day, written short as APR I

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read climbing from bottom to top
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A silly moment for someone deciding to scale a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: APR is the calendar abbreviation for April and I is the Roman one, so APR I is April 1st, the day for fooling people. TO plus C, read upwards, gives COT.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a fruit tree of the plum family, bearing orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Pieces invoking the name of great character

parts.note: pieces and gats are both slang for guns

explanation.surface: Writings that call on the name of a famous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' belongs to the title: Jay Gatsby is the hero of Scott Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby. 'Pieces' means guns, as in gangster slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary reference: the novel's title calls its hero great, so the character in The Great Gatsby is literally a 'great character'.

clue.text: Recruit in growth area giving up employment for navy

indicators.note: giving up something means letting it go, so this piece leaves the word
one thing in for another is a swap, so the navy takes the vacated place

parts.note: a greenhouse is where plants are grown
employment is use, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: A newcomer in horticulture swaps a job for life at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy, the standard crossword abbreviation for the British navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is an inexperienced newcomer, just like a raw recruit.

clue.text: Cut heads on fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone chops the heads off fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb but is a noun: topside is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef, a cut from the butcher.

clue.text: In pubs, one cheers brewer

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: In the pub, a man raises a toast to the brewer of its beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewer' suggests beer to go with pubs and cheers, but a barista brews coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes coffee, and making coffee is brewing it.

clue.text: Clearly show strong desire to break into retail somehow

indicators.note: something that breaks into another thing ends up inside it, so one piece goes inside the other
somehow suggests the letters of retail are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A passionate urge to burgle a shop, put plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retail' looks like shopkeeping, but it is only the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate is to make a point plain by example or picture, demonstrating it clearly.

clue.text: Employee benefit for every last piece of work

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'

indicators.note: the last letter of the word it picks from

explanation.surface: A worker is paid a bonus for every finished job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of work' suggests a finished job, but only the last letter of 'work' is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk, short for perquisite, is a benefit given to an employee beyond pay.

clue.text: Dissertation about unknown number that is somewhere in the UK

indicators.note: about means around, so the dissertation goes round the other pieces

parts.note: x is the unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An academic paper concerning an unspecified figure for a place in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Six Counties is a name for Northern Ireland, the part of the island of Ireland within the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Six Counties is a name, mostly used in Ireland, for Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: At last obtain a garment I will wear, the ultimate in green

indicators.note: the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: I kept as is; as the wearer it goes on before the garment

explanation.surface: A shopper finally gets a green top to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will wear' puts I in front of the VEST it wears. 'Green' is inexperienced, not a colour, so its ultimate is the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive, so the ultimate in green is the most naive, the naivest.

clue.text: Full of vitality, agent recruits a couple of hands

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
the two hands, RIGHT spelt out and L for left

explanation.surface: A lively agent takes on a couple of farmhands.
explanation.walkthrough: The two hands are right and left, one written in full and one abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and energetic, full of vitality.

clue.text: Of course, warning was rejected as expected

parts.note: fore! is the golfer's warning shout on the course

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so WAS is turned round

explanation.surface: Naturally, a warning was ignored, just as everyone knew it would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally' but means on a golf course, where the warning is FORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to see ahead, so foresaw means expected.

clue.text: National Theatre's welcoming days stopped developing

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a whole

explanation.surface: The National Theatre, taking in some new days, has stalled.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Theatre's' is 'has': the theatre has NAT inside it, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop moving or growing, so stagnated is stopped developing.

clue.text: Fine stonework in church choir finally covered by board

indicators.note: something covered by another thing is inside it, so these pieces sit within the board

parts.note: a tray is a flat board for carrying things
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of choir

explanation.surface: Elaborate carving inside a church, with the choir stalls finally boarded over.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the usual crossword church.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is the ornamental stone openwork in the upper part of Gothic windows.

clue.text: Having more showers is way to control foul air rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a rein is a way to control a horse

indicators.note: foul suggests the letters of air are spoilt and jumbled

explanation.surface: A wetter climate is one way to deal with polluted air going up.
explanation.walkthrough: REIN followed by IAR (from 'foul' air) gives REINIAR, which read upwards in the down light becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainier is the comparative of rainy, so it describes weather with more downpours.

clue.text: Roughly struck in the head, rebel falls

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: A rebel, roughly hit on the head, collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like the rebel's verb but is the noun, as in waterfalls. Jack Cade was an English rebel leader of 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, and falls is another name for one.

clue.text: Trick's missed in unreliable moment

indicators.note: something missed in a word is left out of it, so the trick is removed from the longer word

parts.note: a con is a trick; the 's reads as 'is', so 'Trick's missed' is 'trick is missed'

explanation.surface: A fickle moment in which a con trick fails.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Trick's' is 'is': the trick is missed in the word for unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a very brief moment of time.

clue.text: Conclude not a single blazing thing!

parts.note: no means not a single one

explanation.surface: An investigator concludes nothing at all is on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the surprise: the investigator's 'nothing is burning' spells out the very thing that is.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose description rather than a synonym: an inferno is a huge fire, and a fire is a thing that blazes.

clue.text: Help someone easily deceived by reporter

indicators.note: a reporter tells the story out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible person

explanation.surface: A journalist is accused of helping someone who is easily taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reporter' looks like the journalist in the story, but here it only means someone speaking the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help given in time of need.

clue.text: Frame that supports way over lake in part of forest

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the forest part

parts.note: a tree is one part of a forest

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A support structure built for a road over a lake in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'over' stacks one piece above the next, so the way comes before the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a supporting framework, such as the legs holding up a table top or a bridge.

clue.text: It matters little I indicate after noon, provided I withdraw before the finish

indicators.note: after places the indicating word after noon

parts.note: to sign is to indicate, as by a gesture
if means provided, on condition that

indicators.note: before the finish means stopping one letter short of the end

parts.note: to cancel is to withdraw, call off

explanation.surface: A shrug: it hardly matters if I gesture after twelve, if I pull out before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignificance is a small amount of importance, a state of mattering little.

clue.text: Mineral preserved by chemicals

indicators.note: what is preserved by something is kept inside it, so the answer sits inside 'chemicals'

explanation.surface: A mineral sample is kept in a chemical preservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserved by' reads as pickling, but it means the answer is held within the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mica is a mineral that splits into thin shiny sheets.

clue.text: Empty room hottest, a result of breaking this

definitions.text: Empty room hottest, a result of breaking this

indicators.note: an empty room has nothing in it, so only its outer letters R and M remain
the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A room gets as hot as it can once the device controlling it breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a broken thermostat is exactly what leaves an empty room at its hottest.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat regulates temperature, so if it breaks the room can overheat.

clue.text: Start to reel in touchy follower without restraint

indicators.note: in puts this letter inside the follower

parts.note: in the phrase touchy-feely, feely follows touchy

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An angler starts winding in the line with no brake on the reel.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside FEELY after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Freely means without restriction or constraint, at liberty.

clue.text: Order pig to be slaughtered for food

indicators.note: slaughtered letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer sends a pig to be killed for meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The pig suggests pork, but the food is oatmeal boiled in water or milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is a food, a breakfast of oats cooked in milk or water.
